heading: 🌍 Overview
source_blocks.text: New Avalon is a small but technologically superior technocratic micro-nation nestled in the heart of Europe. Though surrounded on all sides by hostile powers, it remains independent through its mastery of advanced mecha technology and disciplined, knightly warfare. Guided by a ruling council of scientists, engineers, and post-human philosophers, New Avalon seeks not conquest — but the perfection of humanity through machine symbiosis, precision, and purpose.

heading: 🏛️ Overview
source_blocks.text: The Iron Concord is a sprawling, militarized feudal empire forged from the ashes of old Europe and Eurasia. Ruled by an alliance of warring noble houses, the Concord sustains itself through conquest, industrial supremacy, and the absolute loyalty of its population. Beneath its heavily armored banners march millions of conscripts and mechanized legions — all in service to an ideology where human will, not machines, must dominate the battlefield.

heading: 🌍 Overview

heading: 🌍 Overview
source_blocks.text: The Fourth Imperium is a militant human theocracy rising from the heart of South America, ruled from Neuform, the holy capital known as The First Seat of Man. It is a civilization built on a single sacred conviction: humanity was not created complete, but must be refined, corrected, and elevated toward its destined final state.

heading: 🌍 Overview
source_blocks.text: Where other powers fight for profit, survival, or sovereignty, the Fourth Imperium wages war as a sacred obligation. Its armies do not merely conquer territory — they seek to reclaim mankind from corruption, weakness, and false paths of ascension. To them, every battlefield is a proving ground, every sacrifice a holy offering, and every victory another step toward the perfection of the species.

heading: 🌍 Overview
source_blocks.text: At the head of the Imperium stands The Ascendant, the supreme temporal and spiritual ruler judged closest to the ideal of the First Form.

heading: 🧠 Philosophy & Society
source_blocks.text: 🧠 Philosophy & Society

heading: 🧠 Philosophy & Society
source_blocks.text: Monolithic Theocracy: Society is governed through the Doctrine of the First Form, a monotheistic state faith centered on humanity’s sacred destiny.

heading: 🧠 Philosophy & Society
source_blocks.text: Perfection Through Correction: Weakness is not merely tolerated or condemned — it is something to be disciplined, purified, or expended in service to the whole.

heading: 🧠 Philosophy & Society
source_blocks.text: The Individual Beneath the Species: Citizens are taught that a single life has value only insofar as it serves mankind’s collective ascent.

heading: 🧠 Philosophy & Society
source_blocks.text: Measured Worth: Purity, discipline, bodily excellence, and loyalty determine status. Rule belongs not to the popular, but to the worthy.

source_blocks.text: ⚔️ Military Doctrine

heading: ⚔️ Military Doctrine
source_blocks.text: Standardized Holy War: The Imperium fields disciplined mass-production war machines built to carry doctrine into battle through force of arms.

heading: ⚔️ Military Doctrine
source_blocks.text: Territorial Crusade: Its main offensives are directed northward against the UNMC, whose corporate rule is denounced as decadent corruption.

heading: ⚔️ Military Doctrine
source_blocks.text: Close Assault & Sacrifice: While many Imperial formations advance in ordered ranks, some branches embrace martyrdom, shock assault, and close-quarters annihilation.

heading: ⚔️ Military Doctrine
source_blocks.text: Measured Command: Even in war, the Imperium seeks order — its officers, judges, and synods direct battle as an extension of sacred law.

heading: 🪖 Faction Profile: The Living Dominion
source_blocks.text: 🪖 Faction Profile: The Living Dominion

heading: 🪖 Faction Profile: The Living Dominion
source_blocks.text: “The flesh remembers. The land endures.”

heading: 🌍 Overview
source_blocks.text: 🌍 Overview

heading: 🌍 Overview
source_blocks.text: The Living Dominion is not a nation in the conventional sense, nor a single people with one capital, one language, or one throne. It is a vast nomadic civilization spread across most of Africa, formed from many older peoples now bound together by a shared way of life known as The Green Path.

heading: 🌍 Overview
source_blocks.text: Where other powers build cities, factories, and fixed borders, the Living Dominion moves in scattered circles that remain in constant communion through living networks of root, spore, beast, and blood. To outsiders, it is a land of vanished expeditions, broken invasions, and impossible monsters. To its own people, it is simply life defending itself.

heading: 🌍 Overview
source_blocks.text: Its most feared guardians are the Warforms — colossal living war-bodies grown, guided, and inhabited by chosen Wardens. These beings are not mindless beasts, nor mere biological machines, but sacred weapons of the Dominion’s will. When foreign armies push too far inland, strip too much from the land, or mistake distance for safety, the Warforms come.

heading: 🌍 Overview
source_blocks.text: Few who meet them survive.

heading: 🧠 Philosophy & Society
source_blocks.text: 🧠 Philosophy & Society

heading: 🧠 Philosophy & Society
source_blocks.text:
Many Peoples, One Path:
 The Dominion is made up of many cultures, lineages, and local traditions, united not by uniformity but by shared survival, mutual duty, and reverence for living systems.

heading: 🧠 Philosophy & Society
source_blocks.text:
The Green Path:
 The Dominion’s guiding philosophy teaches that life endures through balance, adaptation, and cultivation — not domination, extraction, or sterile control.

heading: 🧠 Philosophy & Society
source_blocks.text:
Movement Over Permanence:
 Most of the Dominion lives in small roaming circles rather than permanent cities. These groups travel constantly, tending routes, sacred sites, relay-groves, and living camps.

heading: 🧠 Philosophy & Society
source_blocks.text:
Biology, Not Industry:
 The Dominion is not primitive. It has simply advanced along another path. Its communication, medicine, shelter, and warcraft are grown, cultivated, and symbiotic rather than mechanical.

heading: ⚔️ Military Doctrine
source_blocks.text: ⚔️ Military Doctrine

heading: ⚔️ Military Doctrine
source_blocks.text:
Territory Denial Through Ambush:
 The Living Dominion rarely fights as a conventional front-line state. It lets invaders stretch themselves thin, then strikes with overwhelming force once they are exposed.

heading: ⚔️ Military Doctrine
source_blocks.text:
Warforms as Apex Weapons:
 The Warforms are living engines of war — massive, regenerative, and terrifyingly difficult to put down permanently.

heading: ⚔️ Military Doctrine
source_blocks.text:
Decentralized Warfare:
 The Dominion has no single command center to destroy. Its scattered circles and Wild Hosts can lose ground, vanish, regroup, and strike elsewhere with little warning.

heading: ⚔️ Military Doctrine
source_blocks.text:
Living Infrastructure:
 The same biotech principles that sustain Dominion life also sustain Dominion war. Signals travel through fungal rootwebs, wounds are treated with cultivated organisms, and support systems are alive as surely as the Warforms themselves.

heading: 🧬 Core Faction Rule: Renewal of Flesh
source_blocks.text: 🧬 Core Faction Rule: Renewal of Flesh

heading: 🧬 Core Faction Rule: Renewal of Flesh
source_blocks.text: At the end of each round, before removing destroyed Warforms, roll 1D6 for each friendly Warform that is damaged or destroyed and still represented on the battlefield. On a 6, that Warform regains 1 STR, to a maximum of its starting STR. If a destroyed Warform regains STR this way, it is no longer destroyed, stands up with 1 STR, and becomes Suppressed. A Warform restored by Renewal of Flesh is not treated as a wreck.

heading: 🧬 Core Faction Rule: Renewal of Flesh
🧭 Subfactions – The Four Wild Hosts
source_blocks.text: 🧭 Subfactions – The Four Wild Hosts

heading: 🧭 Subfactions – The Four Wild Hosts
source_blocks.text:
Unlike the subfactions of other powers, the Wild Hosts do not represent rigid political divisions or formal standing armies. They are vast roaming coalitions of Wardens, circles, and Warforms shaped by different histories, frontiers, and philosophies of war.
 All Living Dominion forces use the faction rule Renewal of Flesh rather than separate Wild Host traits.

heading: The World-Treaders
source_blocks.text: The World-Treaders

heading: The World-Treaders
source_blocks.text: The largest and heaviest of the Wild Hosts.

heading: The World-Treaders
source_blocks.text: Their Warforms are vast, brutal, and built for direct territorial denial. When an invasion must be broken by raw force, the World-Treaders answer with enormous living engines that crash through gunlines and fortified positions alike.

heading: The Crown of Ash
source_blocks.text: The Crown of Ash

heading: The Crown of Ash
source_blocks.text: Ancient, saurian, and deeply feared even within the Dominion.

heading: The Crown of Ash
source_blocks.text: This Host fields Warforms that seem less like grown weapons and more like living catastrophes dredged from the world’s oldest memory. Slow, terrible, and relentless, they embody the wrath of the deep earth.

heading: The Veiled Pulse
source_blocks.text: The Veiled Pulse

heading: The Veiled Pulse
source_blocks.text: Fast, precise, and deeply unsettling.

heading: The Veiled Pulse
source_blocks.text: Its Warforms are more humanoid, more controlled, and more uncanny than those of the other Hosts. Many within the Dominion distrust their methods, fearing they stand too close to a path that should never have been walked — yet their loyalty and battlefield value are beyond dispute.

heading: The Ironroot Host
source_blocks.text: The Ironroot Host

heading: The Ironroot Host
source_blocks.text: The most divisive of the Wild Hosts.

heading: The Ironroot Host
source_blocks.text: Where others reject dead machinery, the Ironroot Host is willing to graft, bind, and repurpose limited technological remnants into living flesh. Many see them as dangerously compromised. Others see them as practical defenders willing to use any tool that still serves life.

heading: 🤖 Unit Example: Prowler Warform
source_blocks.text: A mid-sized apex predator bred for pursuit, ambush, and brutal close assault, the Prowler Warform is the shape most invaders encounter first. It lacks the monumental scale of the World-Treaders and the mythic grandeur of the Crown of Ash, but it is faster, more adaptable, and common across all four Wild Hosts.

heading: 🤖 Unit Example: Prowler Warform
source_blocks.text: Its silhouette is low, muscular, and predatory, with heavy forelimbs, layered biological armor, and a cultivated hunting instinct directed by the Warden within. The Prowler is not a sacred relic or rare terror-beast. It is the Dominion’s most practical answer to trespass.

heading: 🌍 Faction Profile: Southern Cross Compact

heading: 🌍 Overview
source_blocks.text: 🌍 Overview

heading: 🌍 Overview
source_blocks.text: The Southern Cross Compact is not a nation, a corporation, or a single army. It is a loose coalition of Australian mercenary companies, salvage syndicates, transport guilds, security contractors, and battlefield recovery crews bound together by contracts, reputation, and necessity.

heading: 🌍 Overview
source_blocks.text: Where the great powers build doctrines, the Compact builds invoices.

heading: 🌍 Overview
source_blocks.text: Their forces are made up of stock mechs bought, leased, salvaged, or captured from the battlefields of the Iron Concord, UN Mega Corporations, and New Avalon. They lack the deep industrial base and technical mastery of the great powers, but make up for it with practical experience, local knowledge, and a culture built around keeping old war machines running one contract at a time.

heading: 🌍 Overview
source_blocks.text: The Southern Cross Compact does not invent the best mechs in the world.

heading: 🌍 Overview
source_blocks.text: It simply knows how to get them, field them, and survive inside them.

heading: 🧠 Philosophy & Society
source_blocks.text: 🧠 Philosophy & Society

heading: 🧠 Philosophy & Society
source_blocks.text: Contract Before Creed: Loyalty lasts as long as the job, the payout, and the odds.

heading: 🧠 Philosophy & Society
source_blocks.text: Coalition of Companies: The Compact is made up of many smaller firms and warbands, not a single central state.

heading: 🧠 Philosophy & Society
source_blocks.text: Salvage Culture: Nothing is wasted if it can still move, shoot, or be sold for parts.

heading: 🧠 Philosophy & Society
source_blocks.text: Pragmatic Warfare: Compact pilots value survival, mobility, and battlefield utility over ideology or honor.

heading: 📦 CONTRACT PROCUREMENT
source_blocks.text: The Southern Cross Compact does not use its own dedicated mech roster in the normal way. Instead, it fields eligible stock mechs hired or acquired from other powers.

heading: 📦 CONTRACT PROCUREMENT

heading: 📦 CONTRACT PROCUREMENT

heading: 🔒 IMPORT RESTRICTIONS
source_blocks.text: 🔒 IMPORT RESTRICTIONS

heading: 🔒 IMPORT RESTRICTIONS
source_blocks.text: When a Southern Cross Compact force includes an imported mech, apply all of the following rules:

heading: 🔒 IMPORT RESTRICTIONS
source_blocks.text:
1. Stock Mechs Only
 Imported mechs must be taken as complete, stock units exactly as listed on their source faction roster.

heading: 🔒 IMPORT RESTRICTIONS
source_blocks.text:
2. No Customization
 Imported mechs may not change their frame, weapons, or systems. They may not purchase alternate faction options, replacement loadouts, or additional armory upgrades unless those options are explicitly part of their stock unit entry.

heading: 🔒 IMPORT RESTRICTIONS
source_blocks.text:
3. No Heroes or Named Units
 The Southern Cross Compact may not include Heroes, named characters, or other Unique faction centerpiece units from another faction.

heading: 🔒 IMPORT RESTRICTIONS
source_blocks.text:
4. Keep the Mech, Lose the Doctrine
 Imported mechs keep their printed weapons, systems, and unit rules on their stock profile, but do not gain:

heading: 🔒 IMPORT RESTRICTIONS
source_blocks.text: source faction core rules

heading: 🔒 IMPORT RESTRICTIONS
source_blocks.text: subfaction traits

heading: 🔒 IMPORT RESTRICTIONS
source_blocks.text: House, Order, Sponsor, or equivalent detachment bonuses

heading: 🔒 IMPORT RESTRICTIONS
source_blocks.text: faction-wide command benefits

heading: 🔒 IMPORT RESTRICTIONS
source_blocks.text: any bonus rule granted for belonging to their original faction as an army

heading: 🔒 IMPORT RESTRICTIONS
source_blocks.text:
5. Faction Identity Changes
 For all army-building and game purposes, imported mechs count as Southern Cross Compact units, not as units of their original faction.

heading: 🔒 IMPORT RESTRICTIONS
source_blocks.text:
6. Source-Locked Benefits Are Lost
 If a rule only functions because the unit belongs to Iron Concord, UNMC, or New Avalon as a faction, that part of the rule is ignored in a Southern Cross Compact force.
